report.source_text: MR image was obtained and showed a small spherical lesion at right subcortical occipital lobe showing different intensities (Fig. 2). Lesion was hypointense on T1-weighted image, hyperintense rim on T2-weighted image. Ring enhancement was noted on the contrast enhanced T1 and blooming artefact on SWI. These findings suggesting granular nodular stage. Other multiple singular lesions were seen at left juxtacortical temporal lobe, right juxtacortical parietal lobe and left thalamus showing different intensities (Figs. 3, and 4). Lesion was also hypointense on T1-weighted image with no signal on T2-weighted image, with blooming artefact on SWI which suggesting nodular calcified stage. No restricted area was seen within the lesion on DWI-ADC on both stages.

report.source_text: MR Spectroscopy was conducted (Fig. 5). Minor shift scale (approximately -0.5 ppm) was made based on major resonances of N-acetylaspartate (NAA), creatine (Cr), and choline (Cho) in the spectroscopy control from the normal parenchyma. Increase in lactate and decrease in choline and N-acetylaspartate were seen which suggesting diagnosis of an inflammatory lesion. Levels of NAA/Cr ratio (0.38) and Cho/Cr ratio (1.21) were seen to be below 1.5.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with intermittent headaches, abrupt vision loss, and left-sided weakness, with a history of stroke one year prior. Initial brain CT revealed multiple calcified nodules (nodular calcified stage) and granular nodular stage lesions in various brain regions. Subsequent MRI confirmed these findings, showing lesions consistent with both granular nodular and nodular calcified stages. MR Spectroscopy indicated an inflammatory lesion with increased lactate and decreased choline and N-acetylaspartate. No serological, CSF, or biopsy confirmation was reported, nor was information on treatment or patient outcome.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: CT brain showed multiple calcified nodules (nodular calcified stage) in right subcortical parietal lobe, left thalamus, left basal ganglia, and granular nodular stage in right cortical-subcortical occipital lobe.

MR image showed a small spherical lesion at right subcortical occipital lobe suggesting granular nodular stage, and multiple singular lesions at left juxtacortical temporal lobe, right juxtacortical parietal lobe and left thalamus suggesting nodular calcified stage.
MR Spectroscopy showed increased lactate and decreased choline and N-acetylaspartate, suggesting an inflammatory lesion.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While there was a history of stroke, the current imaging findings of multiple lesions in different stages (calcified and granular nodular) are not typical for an acute or subacute stroke event, but rather suggest a parasitic infection.

The presence of multiple lesions in different stages (calcified and granular nodular) and the specific MRS findings (increased lactate, decreased NAA/Cr and Cho/Cr ratios below 1.5) are less characteristic of typical brain tumors, which often show elevated choline.
